newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to maintain troops in Bosnia - report.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to maintain troops in Bosnia - report.

text.p: Malaysia will continue to station its troops in Bosnia Herzegovina after the expiry of NATO peace implementation force's (IFOR) mandate in December, a local newspaper reported on Saturday.
"This decision was made at the weekly (cabinet) meeting on Wednesday," Defence Minister Syed Hamid Albar was quoted as saying by the New Straits Times.
"We believe our presence is vital to the reconstruction of the war-torn state," he said.
Syed Hamid said details of the deployment would be known after the meeting between NATO and the new Bosnian government in November.
"We don't know what they require of us. Maybe, they might even request we reduce the size of our contingent or provide some other form of assistance," he said.
Malaysia has more than 1,500 peacekeepers in Bosnia, the third largest contingent after Britain and France.
NATO has said that a follow-up mission, to be called IFOR-2, might be necessary to maintain peace and security in the former Balkan republic.
However, it said the present 60,000 multinational troops would be reduced to about 20,000 under IFOR-2.
